concept.name: Decision journal
concept.definition: A contemporaneous record of the reasoning, expectations, and estimated probabilities behind significant decisions, written before outcomes are known. Its purpose is to make judgment auditable: it counters hindsight bias, enables calibration of forecasts, and separates decision quality from luck.
concept.intuition: Write down what you expect and why before the market answers; later you get to grade your thinking instead of your self-image.
concept.mechanics: For each material decision the trader records the thesis, key assumptions, what would change his mind, and a probability or scenario sketch; at review, predictions are compared with outcomes and with what was actually known at the time. It generalizes the trade-thesis log to all consequential decisions, not only trades.
concept.failure_modes: It is undermined by vague, unfalsifiable entries ('feels bullish') that any outcome can confirm, and by recording probabilities without ever scoring them. The writing cost is real, so it is usually reserved for significant decisions.
concept.misconceptions: A decision journal is not a prediction contest; its value is exposing systematic reasoning errors, not maximizing hit rate. Nor is it only for losing decisions - winning decisions made for bad reasons are the most dangerous to leave unexamined.
concept.example: Before a CPI release a trader logs: '70% odds of a hawkish print; if wrong, expect index -1%; my long is invalid below 5,480.' Post-release review tests both the forecast and the sizing logic.
